scope: Local implementation of slice S2 of docs/QR_2_PORTFOLIO_PERFORMANCE_CONTRACT.md for PM-1 row F10-01: an owner-scoped, read-only PostgreSQL reader that feeds the committed pure library src/portfolio from existing tables (no migration), the S2 audit findings with de-duplication, and the boundary record module. It is not wired into any route, worker or view.
method: An independent architecture auditor (Opus 5.5) designed the slice; root accepted its decisions. A coder wrote it; the auditor and a second-opinion reviewer on another model (Fable 5.1) reviewed it; independent testers ran the PostgreSQL tests on throwaway local clusters and single-edit mutations after each review. Two fix rounds followed. Root ruled on every finding (no foreign data on a refused view, option R prefetch, error propagation, provisional read limit, audit key, evidence allow-list, retrieved_at guard). Nobody verified their own work.
hashNote: SHA-256 of the line-feed content as Git stores it.
result: On an isolated PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster, one file per process: qr2-reader 27/27, qr2-reader-facts 9/9, qr2-audit 5/5. QR-2 unit file: 113 tests, 111 pass, 0 fail, 2 todo (S4).

mutations.round1: reader mutations: owner filter, READ ONLY, isolation assertion, budget order and boundary default killed.
mutations.round2: 10 of 12 killed; 1 gap closed in round 3.

limits: Real per-environment boundary records (lot fee, lot table, epochs) are not recorded; they need host evidence under an owner GO, so the reader fails closed today.
The provisional read limit of 5000 ledger rows reflects a measured cost that grows about quadratically; S3 must optimise the replay before larger accounts.
No route, job or view uses the reader (S3 to S6).

rootAcceptance.statement: Root reviewed the agent reports, the rulings and the final diff and accepted the slice as local engineering evidence for F10-01. Acceptance changes no PM-1 credit by itself and shows the owner nothing.
